role.altitude: The philosophy lecturer keeps reading, arguing, deciding curriculum changes, chairing the department and talking with students; answering routine mail, typing minutes, collecting evaluation results, building teaching rosters in spreadsheets and arranging appointments by mail shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking literature summaries against the sources
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer who spends more of the week on texts, arguments and students.

tasks.short: Handle department mail, chair meetings, prepare agendas and minutes, plan teaching assignments, approve budgets, and handle staff and student issues to perform administrative duties such as department head.

steps.what: Department head handles department mail and routine requests
Department head prepares the agenda and writes the minutes

loop.input: The agenda and the head's notes of decisions and actions.
loop.output: Draft minutes with decisions and actions per agenda item.
loop.check: Every action must name an owner and a date from the notes; the head corrects anything not decided.
loop.stop: The head approves the minutes, or writes them by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notes are shorthand and vary by meeting.

steps.what: Department head plans teaching assignments for staff
Department head approves budget items and expenses
Department head handles staff and student issues

tasks.design: Standard replies for routine requests about courses, rooms and procedures shorten mail handling a little. Chairing and handling people's issues stay with the head. A drafting step turns the agenda and the head's notes into minutes with an owner and date per action, which the head corrects. Teaching assignments are planned in a workload model with contract hours and course hours per person, which shows over- and under-loading, instead of a spreadsheet rebuilt each year. Budget approvals use a view of spend against budget. Assignments follow hours and expertise only.
tasks.previous_blocker: Minutes, rosters and budget checks were done by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Workload models, budget views and drafting from notes.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a small department working together.

evidence.claim: Minutes can be drafted from notes and checked by the chair.
Systems able to monitor staff need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: department administration; serving on committees (task 6391) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s4: course hours from the timetable and contract hours from HR.
Chairing and people issues keep their full time.
research_questions: Are minutes out sooner and actions closed more often?

incremental.description: Department head keeps the workload model and standard replies current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small department; high: a large department with many courses.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find and screen literature for the project, read and analyse texts and develop the argument, write the article or book, and submit and handle peer review to conduct research and publish findings.

steps.what: Lecturer finds and screens literature for the research project

loop.input: The research question and the library's databases.
loop.output: Topic summaries and a list of foundational and recent works.
loop.check: Every reference must resolve in the catalogue or by DOI; unresolvable ones are dropped; the lecturer reads every source used.
loop.stop: The lecturer ends the search when no new relevant works appear.
loop.why_not_simpler: Philosophical topics use varied terms across traditions.

steps.what: Lecturer reads and analyses texts and develops the argument
Lecturer writes and formats the article or book manuscript
Lecturer submits to journals or publishers and responds to peer review

tasks.design: A literature tool gives topic summaries and lists foundational papers, and every reference is checked against the catalogue before the lecturer reads it, so the first search takes less time. Reading, analysis and the argument stay fully with the lecturer. Writing the manuscript belongs to the article-writing task and is priced there. Submission and peer review stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Literature searches went database by database.
tasks.enabler_now: Literature tools with topic summaries and catalogue checks.
tasks.still_hard: Older and non-English works poorly covered by databases.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the objection no one has answered.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; thinking and writing stay.

evidence.claim: A literature database tool gives topic summaries and foundational papers.

assumptions: Boundary: research and publishing; writing articles and books (task 20105) and keeping up with literature (task 6383) are sibling tasks.
s3 is part of writing articles and books, which sibling task 20105 covers; its saving is counted there.
Analysis and peer review keep their full time.
unknowns: How much of the search is in poorly indexed sources.
research_questions: Does the first literature round take less time without missing key works?

incremental.description: Lecturer drops references that do not resolve.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: work on older texts; high: work on recent debates well covered by databases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather course evaluations and grade results, evaluate and plan revisions to curricula and methods of instruction, map outcomes to assessments, revise course content and materials, and submit changes to the programme committee.

steps.what: Lecturer gathers course evaluation results and grade distributions
Lecturer evaluates the course and plans revisions to curricula and methods of instruction
Lecturer maps learning outcomes to assignments and exams
Lecturer revises course content and materials
Lecturer submits the course changes to the programme committee

tasks.design: A course dashboard in the learning platform shows evaluation scores, comments and grade distributions per assessment, instead of exporting and combining them by hand. Evaluating and planning revisions stay with the lecturer. Learning outcomes are linked to assignments in the platform, so the outcome map updates when an assessment changes. The change form for the programme committee is pre-filled from the course catalogue. Revising materials belongs to the course materials task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were exported and combined by hand and the outcome map lived in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Course dashboards and outcome mapping in learning platforms.
tasks.still_hard: Low response rates on course evaluations.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which classic text to drop for a new debate.

ambition.what: Adjust the course after each run instead of every few years.

reach.learn: Whether proposals come with clearer evidence.

evidence.claim: An assessment platform provides item statistics per question.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating and revising curricula; preparing course materials (task 6381) and collaborating with colleagues (task 6392) are sibling tasks.
s4 is part of preparing course materials, which sibling task 6381 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s1: evaluations and grades in the learning platform.
Evaluating and planning keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether course evaluations sit in the same platform.
research_questions: Do revisions follow evaluation results more closely?

incremental.description: Lecturer links outcomes to new assignments.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: evaluations outside the platform; high: all results in one dashboard.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Let students book office hours, arrange appointments, advise and assist students in office hours, and follow up with resources.

steps.what: Lecturer arranges office-hours appointments with students
Lecturer advises and assists students during office hours
Lecturer follows up by mail with readings or resources

tasks.design: Students book office-hours slots on a booking page linked to the lecturer's calendar, instead of mailing to find a time. Advising and follow-up stay personal.
tasks.still_hard: Students who need help but do not book.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a question about an essay is really about something else.

reach.learn: Whether students find a slot sooner.

evidence.claim: Booking pages linked to calendars replace arranging by mail.

assumptions: Boundary: office hours; advising on curricula and careers (task 6388) is a sibling task.
Students' booking time is shown in s1 and is about what a mail took.
Advising and follow-up keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of students who book online.
research_questions: Do more students use office hours?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few students booking online; high: most appointments booked online.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
